# Semantic Evaluation for Text-to-SQL with Distilled Test Suites

[All reading notes](../reading-notes.md) · [Catalog entry](../README.md#test-suites)

**Full paper read · 2026-11-09**

[Original source](https://aclanthology.org/2020.emnlp-main.29.pdf) · EMNLP 2020 proceedings, pages 396-411

**Reading coverage:** All 16 PDF pages: Sections 1-8, Appendix A.1-A.4, Algorithm 1, Tables 1-4, Figures 1-11/captions and references.

## Research question

Approximate semantic SQL equivalence more faithfully than exact-form matching or execution on one database.

## Method

Mutates reference queries into neighbors, samples typed databases respecting declared foreign-key structure and greedily retains tests that distinguish remaining neighbors. The suite is built before seeing submitted model predictions.

## Evaluation

Twenty-one Spider submissions, neighbor discrimination, a 100-case disagreement audit and a separate WikiSQL analysis; suites are supplied for eleven datasets. Adapted comparisons insert gold constants and disregard output-column order.

## What the results support

Multi-database tests expose reference-equivalent queries missed by exact matching and accidental agreements missed by single execution. Appendix A.3 also documents a false positive from an extra predicted predicate.

## Limits and qualifications

Finite gold-centered coverage is not a proof and can miss prediction-only branches. Undeclared domain constraints can make synthetic databases unrealistic. The 100-case audit samples metric disagreements, not arbitrary predictions, and gold-value substitution weakens end-to-end claims.

## Relevance to reliable Text-to-SQL

A foundation for SQL evaluation, with clear separation between approximate equivalence and the correctness of the intended reference.
